summary: Frontend lifecycle test BLOCKED at STEP 1. Sign-in as Line Manager works. Projects tab loads. The '+ New' button opens the CreateProjectWizard. But the 4-step wizard is UNPASSABLE: after filling every Basics field with valid values (name, sector Agriculture, location Lagos, duration 1, unit months, target amount 5000) the 'Continue' button stays aria-disabled='true' with pointer-events:none, so the user (and this test) cannot advance to Step 2. Because Step 1 cannot be completed, none of STEP 2..9 of the lifecycle test could be exercised (no CEO approval, no invite, no investor accept/pay, no PROGRESS, no profit update, no activity feed, no investor financials). Zero backend 4xx/5xx errors were observed on this run — the failure is purely a client-side form-state bug in CreateProjectWizard.

ui_bugs.issue: Continue button on Step 1 is permanently aria-disabled='true' (opacity 0.7, pointer-events:none) even when ALL Basics fields are populated with schema-valid values. Confirmed via localStorage 'ribhshare:project-draft' that all values reach the Zustand draft store correctly (name, sector, location, durationValue='1', targetAmount='5000', durationUnit='MONTHS'). But basicsMethods.formState.isValid stays false in the wizard component, so the Continue Button (from src/components/ui/Button.tsx) receives disabled=true. This blocks the entire wizard — no way to create a project.

Clicking Months/Weeks/Days chip calls methods.setValue('durationUnit', unit) WITHOUT { shouldValidate: true, shouldDirty: true }. Since durationUnit is a required schema field but is never mutated through a Controller's onChange, RHF never re-runs zod validation after the chip is toggled. This is the most likely reason formState.isValid stays false.

basicsMethods = useForm({ defaultValues: {} }). Because defaults are empty, RHF starts formState.isValid=false. If the wizard also fails to subscribe to isValid via the RHF proxy re-render (or if any Controller field never fires onChange because RN-Web input events don't bubble through FormInput/TextInput correctly), the flag will never become true. Recommend defaultValues = draft.basics AND passing `mode: 'onChange'` + explicit `trigger()` when the chip is pressed.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot progress past wizard Step 1, so NONE of the requested lifecycle assertions could be verified: CEO approval, invitation, investor accept/commit/proof, PROGRESS auto-transition, profit update posting/summary, activity feed, investor financials tab, portfolio aggregation. All these need re-testing after the Continue-button bug is fixed.

action_items: PRIMARY FIX: In /app/src/screens/projects/steps/CreateProjectStepBasics.tsx, change the chip onPress to: `onPress={() => methods.setValue('durationUnit', unit, { shouldValidate: true, shouldDirty: true, shouldTouch: true })}`. This will force RHF to re-run zod validation and flip formState.isValid to true.

SECONDARY FIX: In /app/src/screens/projects/CreateProjectWizard.tsx L64-68, initialise basicsMethods with `defaultValues: draft.basics` (same as detailsMethods does with draft.details) so the RHF form starts pre-populated when the user resumes a draft AND so isValid can evaluate immediately.
Consider adding a useEffect in CreateProjectStepBasics that calls `methods.trigger()` on mount, so the form is validated once even without any change events.
Consider showing 'Fix required fields' hint under the disabled Continue button — currently the user has no feedback why the button isn't advancing.
After the wizard fix ships, RE-RUN the complete STEP 1..9 lifecycle test — none of it was reachable in this iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: React-hook-form + RN-Web + Controller pattern is fragile: any setValue call that skips shouldValidate will leave isValid stale. Grep the entire codebase for `setValue(` and ensure `{ shouldValidate: true }` is passed wherever the value affects gate-keeping UI (Continue/Submit buttons).

The pattern of gating Continue via `basicsMethods.formState.isValid` while ALSO persisting values through a separate `methods.watch()` -> draft store subscription is duplicative and error-prone. Consider having the wizard read directly from the draft store and drop the double bookkeeping.

CreateProjectWizard.tsx has `require-cycle` warning: `CreateProjectWizard -> CreateProjectStepDocuments -> CreateProjectWizard`. Move REQUIRED_SLOTS constant to a shared file (e.g. src/constants/documents.ts).

Console noise: 'Too many screens defined. Route "invitations/[id]" is extraneous', 'projects/[id]' extraneous — expo-router layout has duplicated Screen declarations. Clean up /app/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx.

The Button component (src/components/ui/Button.tsx) applies opacity 0.7 when disabled BUT keeps the primary-green background — visually it does NOT read as disabled. Change disabled styling to muted grey background so user gets feedback.

No client-side error message is shown for form validation failures on Basics — the user sees no red text under fields. Enable RHF's error rendering in FormInput or make the Continue button show a tooltip listing what's missing.

rca of the issue: Root cause: /app/src/screens/projects/steps/CreateProjectStepBasics.tsx invokes `methods.setValue('durationUnit', unit)` WITHOUT `{ shouldValidate: true }`. React-hook-form's `setValue` intentionally does NOT re-run validation unless explicitly asked to. Since durationUnit is a REQUIRED zod field and it is only ever set via the chip (never via a Controller's onChange), RHF never has a chance to validate that field and never marks it as valid. As a result `basicsMethods.formState.isValid` stays false, `canProceedToNextStep()` returns false, and the Continue button receives disabled=true forever — regardless of what the user types elsewhere. Reproduction (deterministic on preview URL): sign in as LM, /projects > + New, fill all fields, tap months chip, click Continue → nothing happens. Fix: change the chip onPress to `methods.setValue('durationUnit', unit, { shouldValidate: true, shouldDirty: true, shouldTouch: true })`. Also consider `useEffect(() => { methods.trigger(); }, [methods])` in CreateProjectStepBasics to validate on mount when resuming a persisted draft. Zero backend 4xx/5xx responses were observed during the test, so the previously-reported Supabase RPC/migration issues appear resolved on this run — but they could not be verified end-to-end because the wizard blocks all downstream flows.
